findings.text: The kind rule also proves the claim for every input without splitting on whether the key is taken, as Lean accepts a proof that establishes readiness and splits on `insertOutcome`. Fix: record the kind-rule result alongside the case-type result, with 32 code lines for the helper and 11 for the unchanged client claim under the same counting convention.

Only `runScriptStep_insert_ok` takes `InsertFits`, while `runScriptStep_insert_failed` requires the readiness checks and an error outcome. Fix: attribute the `InsertFits` shortcut to the success law and state the failure law’s premises separately.

The task requires the derivability and line cost for each form, but the comparison leaves the kind rule from the case type unresolved. Fix: record the Lean-checked 21-line proof that applies `runScriptStep_plainInsert_of_case` and constructs the case of the rule’s right-hand side, while noting that the current cover theorem itself depends on the kind rule.

The record says the cover theorem needs a statement variable, but Lean accepts the full `insert_any_case` proof with the concrete INSERT supplied as `statement` and the resolution premise closed by `rfl`. Fix: describe `generalize` as the fixture’s way to avoid repeating the concrete syntax.

The totals of 79, 75 and 69 count `items_taken_outcome` but omit other helper theorems used by the same proofs, including the 18-line `items_fits` and 23-line `items_ready`. Fix: label these numbers as subtotals and report the shared helper lines separately so the owner can recover the full client cost.

Both `insertCounts_error_changes` and `insertCounts_error_total` have three statement lines through `:= rfl`, but the table counts the following blank line for each. Fix: change both entries to 3 and the statement-line sum to 49.

The record and status claim to cover every code-changing commit, but omitted revisions include `7dbeba93`, which introduced the case laws, and `24d517a0`, which added the case-type client test. Fix: describe the table and the status at line 30 as measurements of selected milestone revisions.

The claim that the case laws change no declaration from the start revision contradicts the record’s own measurement that `runScriptStep_insert_ok` went from 34 code lines to 22. Fix: narrow the claim to the pre-existing callers counted in this section and identify the restored success theorem separately.

The measurement table claims to source every number, but the caller counts use the unlisted `decl_diff.py` and the statement of `StepCase.unique` was counted by hand. Fix: identify the table as the main measurement scripts and retain the specific sources beside the exceptions.
